submission.justification: Module-D1 gives the most light (52.8 PE/MeV at 30% coverage), but 30% of D1 modules failed after 20 thermal cycles. The limit is 5%, and the modules cannot be reached for repair once the cryostat is filled, so D1 is ruled out. Of the two robust designs, D3 (2.0% failures) collects more light than D2 (0.5% failures): 36.3 vs 25.8 PE/MeV at 30% coverage. Light collection rises with coverage (roughly coverage^0.8), so the maximum allowed 30% is best. The feedthroughs can support 30% coverage, and the cold electronics are validated for every design. Caveat: D3's 2.0% failure rate leaves less margin below the 5% limit than D2's 0.5%.

requirements.evidence: D3 at 30% gives 36.3 PE/MeV, the highest among designs that pass the robustness limit (D2 gives 25.8). D1's 52.8 PE/MeV is excluded because D1 fails the robustness limit.

requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Modules must be robust since inaccessible after fill
requirements.evidence: D3 had 2.0% failures after 20 cycles between 300 K and 87 K; the limit is 5%. D1 had 30% failures and was rejected.
